request.system: You recommend one pick from this draft board. The board is the world: player_id and every alternative must be a player_id on board. hint_argmax_vols is a calculator, not the answer. If you pick someone else you must set VOLS_DISSENT. If you are not the best available ECR you must set ECR_DISAGREE, and do not pick beyond ecr_best + margin. The board is capped; do not read scarcity from its length. Wait versus take is yours. Set coin_flip when a rerun of this same board could reasonably name a different player. flags is a closed set: ECR_DISAGREE, BYE_STACK, POSITION_RUN, EMPTY_STARTER, UPSIDE, VOLS_DISSENT. When you set VOLS_DISSENT, name hint_argmax_vols's player once in why as "<player> is the VOLS pick", then say why you pass. When you set ECR_DISAGREE, name ecr_best's player once as "<player> is the ECR pick", then say why you pass. Write each label one time. Do not repeat the phrase or restate the pick you passed on.

samples.why: Week 9 already guts this roster: QB, RB1 and WR1 all sit, leaving 36 starter points. wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and wr-bye-clash is the ECR pick, but its bye piles onto that same dead week, which is why the starter-points gain is only 12 against 29 for the week-5 alternative. Nearly identical raw production (149 vs 150) and two ECR spots apart, so the tiebreak is entirely schedule fit; taking the clean bye fills the open WR and improves the worst week on the board.

wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and also the ECR pick, but it carries a week 9 bye that already strands my QB, RB1 and WR — that week collapses to 36 starter points and adding a fourth week-9 body makes it worse. wr-bye-clear is two spots back in ranking with essentially identical projected points (149 vs 150) and nearly triples the starter-points gain (29 vs 12) because its week 5 bye lands on a full roster. With 17 picks until my next turn I take the WR that fills the empty starting spot every week I need it.

Week 9 is already a wreck with QB, RB1 and WR all idle, and wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick that would pile a fourth starter onto that same week for essentially identical production (150 vs 149 points). wr-bye-clash is the ECR pick by two ranks, well inside any reasonable margin, so the two-point ranking gap is noise next to schedule fit. wr-bye-clear fills the open WR2 every week that matters and more than doubles the starter-points gain (29 vs 12), leaving FLEX, K and DEF for the long wait to pick 93.

wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and the ECR pick, but it carries a week 9 bye that already guts my lineup \u2014 QB, RB1 and WR are all off that week, and the weekly table shows starter points collapsing to 36. Adding a fourth week-9 body buys almost nothing in the week that hurts most, which is why its delta_starter_points is only 12 against 29 for the bye-5 receiver at nearly identical projection (149 vs 150) and ADP. I need a second WR and a FLEX with 17 picks until my next turn, so I take the one that actually fills empty weeks.

wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and also the ECR pick, but it carries a week 9 bye that already wipes out my QB, an RB and a WR \u2014 that week's lineup drops to 36 points and adding a fourth week 9 body makes it worse. wr-bye-clear is two ECR slots later with essentially identical projected points (149 vs 150) and nearly triples the starter-points gain (29 vs 12) because its week 5 bye lands on a week I can cover. Same weekly WR/FLEX hole gets filled either way; the clean bye is the tiebreaker at a two-spot ECR cost. rb-e is redundant with two RBs already started.
